newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan central bank tries novel "closed" injection.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan central bank tries novel "closed" injection.

text.p: The central bank on Tuesday used a novel closed approach to inject T$20 billion into Taiwan's liquidity-strapped banking system, allowing a state-run bank to withdraw money it had redeposited in the central bank.
The central bank agreed to let state-run Taiwan Cooperative Bank make the withdrawal to increase money market liquidity as short-term rates soared, a central bank official said.
The unprecedented move followed central bank assurances late on Monday that it would not inject funds through open market operations to loosen up tight liquidity.
That comment, issued by central bank banking department chief Li Sheng-yen, sent Taiwan's money rates surging further on Tuesday on expectations that liquidity would tighten further, dealers said.

Dealers said the method of Tuesday's fund injection had not been seen before, calling it a "closed market operation". To withdraw such redeposits in the central bank must gain special approval by the central bank, dealers said.

At 0400 GMT, the overnight interbank rate had rocketed to 9.103 percent against Monday's 8.323 close -- far outside the central bank's target zone of 5.0-5.5 percent -- with 30-day commercial paper soaring to 8.00-8.75 against 7.50-7.75.
By 0750 GMT, the overnight rate had drifted lower to 8.375 percent after the market learned of the unusual fund injection, dealers said.
